stage: warning-blind connectivity precision validation Phase M
conclusion: The historical monotone connectivity interpretation is rejected. At high precision m=0.20 returns to R4 and shows no excess block heterogeneity. m=0.10 remains R3 and shows detectable between-block rate heterogeneity, driven by one 66/93=0.710 block, while pooled loss and paired marginal loss probability remain essentially unchanged. Allele-frequency mixing can therefore alter stochastic block dependence at a specific tested level, but is not a monotone rescue/collapse axis and does not show a directional marginal-risk effect across the tested levels.
